episodes.207350: A strong cold front moved through the region during the early morning hours.  Instability was confined to right along the coast, but a line of storms developed along the coast with one supercell ahead of the line. This storm produced two tornadoes near Mexico Beach.
episodes.207351: A strong cold front moved through the region during the early morning hours of October 27th with a secondary front on October 29th. A tornadic waterspout developed offshore of Mexico Beach and moved onshore as a tornado during the early morning hours off October 27th.  Gusty winds occurred with the frontal passage on October 29th.
episodes.207390: A line of showers and thunderstorms associated with a cold front moving southeast across the peninsula extending from a developing frontal wave along the Southeast U.S. coast produce a few strong marine wind gusts across Tampa Bay area waters.
episodes.207391: A line of showers and thunderstorms associated with a cold front moving southeast across the peninsula extending from a developing frontal wave along the Southeast U.S. coast produce a damaging wind gust near Port Richey in Pasco County.
episodes.207560: Isolated gale-force wind gusts occurred in association with fast-moving convective showers embedded in a tight lower tropospheric pressure gradient between a large area of high pressure along the U.S. east coast and Hurricane Melissa over the central Caribbean Sea.
episodes.207678: A F0 tornado touched down near Rigby with damage reported.
episodes.207915: Thunderstorms developed across the area and one storm produced an EF-1 tornado in Baldwin county.
episodes.207916: A thunderstorm produced large hail in Escambia County.
episodes.207985: A strong thunderstorm dropped three-quarter diameter hail over parts of Douglas County between 5:00 PM and 6:00 PM.
episodes.207998: Stationary thunderstorms produced extreme rainfall in Brevard and Lake Counties, as well as a severe wind gust along the coast.
episodes.207999: Thunderstorms produced widespread strong to severe wind gusts along the east central Florida coast.
episodes.208001: Thunderstorms produced gusty winds along and offshore from the Brevard and Treasure Coasts.
episodes.208276: A short-lived waterspout/landspout was reported near the U.S. Coast Guard Station in South Padre Island. This waterspout/landspout caused some minor damage to a small building.
episodes.208419: A frontal boundary retreating across South Florida and ample low-level tropical moisture allowed for showers and thunderstorms to produce excessive rainfall on the evening of October 26 into the early overnight of October 27 which led to flooding over portions of Southeast Florida.

An additional stalled thunderstorm formed over Sharpes and Cocoa, where it produced approximately 6 to 8 inches of rainfall. A portion of US-1 just south of Port St John was washed out near Spring St, as well as multiple segments of Indian River Dr. between Blacks Rd. and City Point Rd. At least 60 homes and businesses were affected, with 50 reporting minor to major damage due to water entering structures. This was part of a rare, high-impact flood event that also impacted Tiusville, Mims, and north Merritt Island, with a 12-hour annual exceedance probability (AEP or the percent chance of an event occurring in any calendar year) between 0.5% and 0.2%, alternatively known as a 200 to 500-year rainfall event.

A stalled thunderstorm produced between 6 to 12 inches of rainfall over portions of north Merritt Island. Flash flooding lead to numerous roads being flooded, including Nina Court. According to local emergency managers, over 150 homes and businesses were affected by flooding, including one house with major damage and over 90 with minor damage, due to floodwaters entering structures. This was part of a rare, high-impact flood event that also impacted Tiusville, Mims, Sharpes, and Cocoa, with a 12-hour annual exceedance probability (AEP or the percent chance of an event occurring in any calendar year) between 0.5% and 0.2%, alternatively known as a 200 to 500-year flood.

The tornado touched down just south of the intersection of Kleinschmidt Road and County Road 87, where minor tree damage was observed. Traveling to the northeast, the tornado crossed County Road 87, uprooting a couple of trees and removing portions of the roof from a small barn. The tornado continued to the northeast before strengthening along Woerner Road South. Here, a large barn lost much of its metal roof paneling, and several trees were uprooted. The tornado appears to have lifted before crossing Woerner Road.||October 29th update: Additional drone video was provided along County Road 87 that revealed the path width being close to 125 yards and an additional patch of trees within a tree stand behind the ground surveyed properties that had several skinny pine trees snapped low bringing the intensity to 95mph.||Special thanks to the Baldwin County EMA for their assistance with this survey.||After review of available high-resolution satellite imagery, the tornado was found to have begun slightly earlier in the forest to the south of Kleinschmidt Road. The tornado was also found to have turned to the east as it crossed Woerner Road South where it did minor tree damage before lifting.
Portions of West Cypress Creek Road were impassable due to flash flooding. Numerous other roads in the area also experienced flooding.

A short-lived landspout/waterspout nudged over the sand flats about 200 yards southeast of the U.S. Coast Guard station, and ripped apart a small building housing a generator near the aerostat dirigible located there. An instantaneous 20-foot wind gusts of 47 mph was reported at that site, which was less than 100 feet from the damaged structure. A wind gusts of 33.82 knots was recorded at the nearby Brazos Santiago platform, 0.5 miles to the east. Confirmation of the landspout/waterspout was provided by night camera video.

events.county: Coastal Waters From Okaloosa-Walton County Line To Mexico Beach Out 20Nm
events.narrative: A tornadic waterspout moved onshore in Mexico Beach and continued as an EF1 tornado through Mexico Beach.
An Ambient weather station in Mexico Beach gusted to 58 mph.

Straight line wind damage occurred to the southeast of an EF1 tornado due to the rear flank downdraft of the supercell.  Winds were estimated around 75 mph.  Damage to roofing and siding occurred to homes.

A tornadic waterspout moved onshore into Mexico Beach at approximately 6:30 am CDT, causing roof and siding damage to a couple of homes along the beach. The roof of the El Governor hotel was lifted and tossed across U.S. 98 into an RV park, where several RV's were damaged or rolled over. A number of minor injuries were reported at the RV park. The tornado continued eastward, moving inland across several neighborhoods.  Roof damage, the most significant of which involved the peeling of metal roofing, was noted at several locations. Otherwise, the damage was scattered and mostly minor. The tornado dissipated before reaching Highway 386. The damage was consistent was an EF1 tornado with maximum winds of approximately 100 mph.

A very brief tornado tracked across U.S. Highway 98, damaging fencing and signs in a new construction neighborhood. The fencing was blown from east to west across the highway. No structural damage was noted and the damage appeared consistent with an EF0 tornado with maximum winds of approximately 70 mph.
